caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:001285
attempts.paper_title: Electroencephalogram signatures of loss and recovery of consciousness from propofol
attempts.entry_title: EEG signatures of loss and recovery of consciousness from propofol (Purdon et al. 2013)
attempts.summary: None of the paper's main findings could be tested in this data, because the dandiset holds the EEG of one of the ten volunteers and none of the task data. The loss of response to clicks before verbal stimuli, the timing of unconsciousness, the beta and gamma rise before it, the frontal alpha mode and the phase-amplitude shift all need the button-press responses, which are not deposited. The 64 channels also lack names and positions, so spatial results cannot be built. All 22 claims were blocked, and none reproduced or failed. The one subject's band-power course tests no claim.
attempts.description: Checks dandiset 001285 against the findings of Purdon et al. (2013) on behaviour and EEG during gradual propofol induction and emergence in 10 volunteers. The dandiset holds the 64-channel EEG of one subject, without channel names, behavioural responses, infusion levels or time markers, so none of the paper's 22 claims can be tested; the notebook describes the file and checks it against its description.

outcomes.statement: In all 10 subjects, during induction, the probability of response to clicks was below that to verbal stimuli in the transition between EON and LOC.
outcomes.source: Results, Continuous Transitions Between Consciousness and Unconsciousness, paragraph 2; Figure 1C
outcomes.quote: During induction, in 10 of 10 subjects, we observed that Pclicks < Pverbal during the transition between EON and LOC
outcomes.notes: Needs each subject's time series of responses to the click and verbal stimuli. The NWB file holds no stimuli, button presses, trials, events or intervals, and the dandiset holds 1 of the 10 subjects. Searched the file (every group), the dandiset's assets (one file), and DANDI for other dandisets of the study (001286 and 001287 carry the same description and hold no files).

outcomes.statement: The transition from EON to LOC took a median of 23.9 min across subjects (range 6.7 to 32.8 min, quartiles 16.4 and 28.6 min).
outcomes.source: Results, Continuous Transitions Between Consciousness and Unconsciousness, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: The transition between EON and LOC required a median of 23.9 min (minimum, 6.7 min; 25th percentile, 16.4 min; 75th percentile, 28.6 min; maximum 32.8 min)
outcomes.notes: EON and LOC are defined from the response-probability curves, and the responses are not in the dandiset (see fig1c-clicks-lost-before-verbal). The file holds no time markers either, and only 1 of 10 subjects, so the across-subject median and quartiles cannot be formed.

outcomes.statement: At the group level, aligned at LOC, Pclicks was below Pverbal during the transition to LOC, and the difference grew as subjects approached LOC.
outcomes.source: Results, Continuous Transitions Between Consciousness and Unconsciousness, paragraph 2; Figure 1 D and E
outcomes.quote: The group-level analysis corroborated the individual subject analyses, showing that Pclicks < Pverbal during the transition to LOC (Pr{Pclicks < Pverbal} > 0.95; Fig. 1E). Moreover, the group-level curves showed a gradual increase in the difference between these response probabilities as subjects approached LOC
outcomes.notes: The group curves pool the responses of 10 subjects aligned at LOC; no responses are deposited and 9 of 10 subjects are absent.

outcomes.statement: During emergence, at the group level aligned at ROC, Pclicks was below Pverbal, while individual curves were more variable.
outcomes.source: Results, Continuous Transitions Between Consciousness and Unconsciousness, paragraph 3; Figure 1E
outcomes.quote: During emergence, individual response-probability curves were more variable, but again we found that Pclicks < Pverbal at the group level
outcomes.notes: As fig1e-group-induction, aligned at ROC.

outcomes.statement: During emergence 6 of 10 subjects did not reach EOFF, as Pclicks did not stay above 0.95 for 5 min or longer.
outcomes.source: Results, Continuous Transitions Between Consciousness and Unconsciousness, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: During emergence, 6 of 10 subjects did not reach EOFF because they did not achieve Pclicks > 0.95 for 5 min or longer
outcomes.notes: EOFF is defined from Pclicks, which needs the responses to the click stimuli, not in the dandiset; the count is over 10 subjects, of which 1 is deposited.

outcomes.statement: The transition from ROC to EOFF (or the end of the recording when EOFF was not reached) took a median of 25.5 min (range 4.9 to 47.6 min, quartiles 12.8 and 38.0 min).
outcomes.source: Results, Continuous Transitions Between Consciousness and Unconsciousness, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: We found that the transition between ROC and EOFF required a median of 25.5 min (minimum, 4.9 min; 25th percentile, 12.8 min; 75th percentile, 38.0 min; maximum, 47.6 min)
outcomes.notes: ROC and EOFF come from the responses, not in the dandiset; 1 of 10 subjects.

outcomes.statement: Gamma and beta power rose significantly above baseline in the 30 min before LOC and stayed elevated during unconsciousness.
outcomes.source: Results, Dynamics of the EEG Spectrum Covary with Changes in Probability of Response and LOC/ROC, paragraph 1; Figure 2 B and C
outcomes.quote: gamma (25–40 Hz) and beta (13–24Hz) power increased significantly above baseline levels during the 30 min before LOC ... and remained elevated during the unconscious period

statistics.test: sign test at each time-frequency location

outcomes.notes: The spectrogram is aligned at LOC, which the paper derives from the behavioural responses (not deposited), and significance is a sign test across 10 subjects (1 deposited). The channel near Fz and the Laplacian also cannot be formed, as the 64 channels have no names or positions (metadata_insufficient). In the deposited subject, beta power (median over the 64 unnamed channels) steps to about 2 times the first 15 min of the file at minute 17 and to 5.5 to 9.9 times (median 7.6 over minutes 33 to 47) at minute 33, which describes the file and tests nothing.

outcomes.statement: At LOC, alpha (8 to 12 Hz) and low-frequency (0.1 to 1 Hz) power both increased significantly.
outcomes.source: Results, Dynamics of the EEG Spectrum Covary with Changes in Probability of Response and LOC/ROC, paragraph 1; Figure 2 B and C
outcomes.quote: At LOC, both alpha (8–12 Hz) and low-frequency (0.1–1 Hz) power increased significantly

statistics.test: sign test at each time-frequency location

outcomes.notes: Needs LOC (from the responses, not deposited) and the sign test across 10 subjects (1 deposited); the channel near Fz cannot be identified (no channel names or positions; metadata_insufficient).

outcomes.statement: Fifteen minutes after LOC, the alpha power increase was concentrated in frontal channels and the low-frequency increase was spread broadly over temporal and parietal channels.
outcomes.source: Results, Dynamics of the EEG Spectrum Covary with Changes in Probability of Response and LOC/ROC, paragraph 1; Figure 2D
outcomes.quote: Fifteen minutes after LOC, the increases in alpha power were concentrated in frontal channels, whereas those for low-frequency power were distributed broadly across temporal and parietal channels
outcomes.notes: Needs LOC (not deposited) and the median map across 10 subjects (1 deposited). The channel groups (frontal, temporal, parietal, occipital) also cannot be formed, as the channels have no names or positions (metadata_insufficient).

outcomes.statement: During emergence the changes reversed with a similar time course, frontal alpha and low-frequency power decreasing at ROC while gamma and beta power stayed elevated after ROC.
outcomes.source: Results, Dynamics of the EEG Spectrum Covary with Changes in Probability of Response and LOC/ROC, paragraph 1; Figure 2 B and C
outcomes.quote: During emergence, these changes in power occurred in reverse, following a similar time course: Frontal alpha and low-frequency power decreased at ROC, whereas gamma/beta power remained elevated throughout the post-ROC period when Pclicks < Pverbal

statistics.test: sign test at each time-frequency location

outcomes.notes: Needs ROC and EOFF (from the responses, not deposited) and the sign test across 10 subjects (1 deposited); no channel names for Fz (metadata_insufficient).

outcomes.statement: Low-frequency power increased more than 10-fold in the unconscious state compared with baseline.
outcomes.source: Results, Changes in Spatially Coherent Alpha Activity Mark Unconsciousness, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: low-frequency power increased by more than 10-fold in the unconscious state compared with baseline
outcomes.notes: The claim's quantity is the group median across 10 subjects of low-frequency power in the unconscious state (between LOC and ROC, or at LOC + 15 min) over baseline, at the channel near Fz or over channels. LOC and ROC are not deposited, 9 of 10 subjects are absent, and the channels have no names (metadata_insufficient). As a description of the file only, low-frequency power, median over the 64 unnamed channels without a Laplacian, is 6.5 to 34 times its level in the first 15 min from minute 49 to minute 97 (median 15.4 over minutes 60 to 100; 16.3 over the 55 channels with SDs below 300 uV). The reference period was chosen after looking at the data, and the period is not shown to be the unconscious state, so this is no evidence for the claim.

outcomes.statement: In the transition before LOC, the median frequency of the frontal spectrum fell from 23.1 to 12.0 Hz and its bandwidth (interquartile range) from 17.4 to 9.1 Hz.
outcomes.source: Results, Dynamics of the EEG Spectrum Covary with Changes in Probability of Response and LOC/ROC, paragraph 3; Figure 3A
outcomes.quote: During induction, in the transition period before LOC, the median frequency decreased from 23.1 to 12.0 Hz, and the bandwidth decreased from 17.4 to 9.1 Hz
outcomes.notes: Needs the group spectrogram aligned at LOC, with the start of the transition at EON or 30 min before LOC; LOC and EON come from the responses, not deposited, and 9 of 10 subjects are absent. No channel names for Fz (metadata_insufficient).

outcomes.statement: In the transition after ROC, the median frequency rose from 11.8 to 21.9 Hz and the bandwidth from 9.9 to 12.8 Hz.
outcomes.source: Results, Dynamics of the EEG Spectrum Covary with Changes in Probability of Response and LOC/ROC, paragraph 3; Figure 3A
outcomes.quote: During emergence, in the transition period after ROC, the median frequency increased from 11.8 to 21.9 Hz, and the bandwidth increased from 9.9 to 12.8 Hz
outcomes.notes: As fig3a-induction-traveling-peak, aligned at ROC with EOFF; neither is deposited.

outcomes.statement: Power at the median frequency had a frontal distribution at each behavioral time point.
outcomes.source: Results, Dynamics of the EEG Spectrum Covary with Changes in Probability of Response and LOC/ROC, paragraph 4; Figure 3B
outcomes.quote: We found that the power at the median frequency had a frontal distribution across the different behavioral time points
outcomes.notes: Needs all seven behavioural time points (from the responses, not deposited), the group median across 10 subjects (1 deposited), and channel groups, which cannot be formed without channel names or positions (metadata_insufficient).

outcomes.statement: Gamma and beta power were frontal from Pre-LOC through LOC; during unconsciousness the frontal power moved into the beta and alpha bands; during emergence it shifted back toward beta and gamma, and frontal gamma power persisted through EOFF.
outcomes.source: Results, Dynamics of the EEG Spectrum Covary with Changes in Probability of Response and LOC/ROC, paragraph 4; Figure S2
outcomes.quote: Gamma and beta power showed a frontal distribution from Pre-LOC through LOC; during unconsciousness the frontal power distribution moved to the beta and alpha bands ... In addition, frontal gamma power appeared to persist through EOFF
outcomes.notes: As fig3b-frontal-median-frequency-power; the frontal and occipital groups cannot be formed either.

outcomes.statement: At baseline the principal mode of the alpha band is spatially coherent over occipital channels; its modal projection dissipates at LOC and returns at ROC, remaining prominent after ROC.
outcomes.source: Results, Changes in Spatially Coherent Alpha Activity Mark Unconsciousness, paragraph 2; Figure 4 A and B
outcomes.quote: Occipital prominence of the principal mode was present while the subjects were awake, ended at LOC, and returned, and remained prominent after ROC

statistics.test: permutation test (circular time shifts, 200 permutations resampled 500 times)

outcomes.notes: The timing part needs LOC and ROC (not deposited) and the group mean over 10 subjects (1 deposited). The spatial part, whether the baseline mode is occipital, needs channel positions or names, which the file does not hold (metadata_insufficient); the full baseline period is not marked either.

outcomes.statement: During unconsciousness the principal alpha mode (about 10 Hz) is spatially coherent over frontal channels; its modal projection begins after LOC and ceases at ROC.
outcomes.source: Results, Changes in Spatially Coherent Alpha Activity Mark Unconsciousness, paragraph 2; Figure 4 C and D
outcomes.quote: Activity within this frontal alpha mode, characterized by the modal projection, begins after LOC and ceases at ROC ... during unconsciousness, the principal mode in the alpha range was prominent in a frontal distribution

statistics.test: permutation test (circular time shifts, 200 permutations resampled 500 times)

outcomes.notes: The unconscious cross-spectral matrix is taken from LOC to ROC (not deposited); group over 10 subjects (1 deposited); frontal channels cannot be identified (no names or positions; metadata_insufficient).

outcomes.statement: Low frequencies showed no prominent principal mode, although low-frequency power rose more than 10-fold in unconsciousness.
outcomes.source: Results, Changes in Spatially Coherent Alpha Activity Mark Unconsciousness, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: In contrast, low frequencies did not show a prominent principal mode
outcomes.notes: The paper's test uses the unconscious mode between LOC and ROC and the group mean over 10 subjects; LOC and ROC are not deposited and 9 of 10 subjects are absent. The test is that of fig4cd-frontal-alpha-mode, defined as fig4ab-occipital-alpha-mode, which applies the Laplacian (the paper applies it to "this and subsequent analyses"); the Laplacian needs channel names or positions, which the file does not hold (metadata_insufficient).

outcomes.statement: From about 20 min before LOC to about 10 min after it, alpha/beta (8 to 14 Hz) amplitude was largest at the troughs of the low-frequency (0.1 to 1 Hz) oscillation (trough-max), significant in 9 of 10 subjects within 10 min of LOC.
outcomes.source: Results, Different Patterns of Phase-Amplitude Modulation, paragraph 2; Figure 5 B and C
outcomes.quote: During induction, beginning ∼20 min before LOC and extending ∼10 min after LOC, the alpha/beta amplitudes were largest at the troughs of low-frequency oscillations (Fig. 5 B and C; P < 0.05 in 9 of 10 subjects within 10 min of LOC by permutation test
outcomes.notes: The epochs are placed relative to LOC (not deposited) and the count is over 10 subjects (1 deposited); the frontal channel near Fz and its Laplacian cannot be formed without channel names or positions (metadata_insufficient).

outcomes.statement: During profound unconsciousness, 10 to 40 min after LOC, the modulation shifted by 180 degrees, alpha/beta amplitude being largest at low-frequency peaks (peak-max), significant in 8 of 10 subjects.
outcomes.source: Results, Different Patterns of Phase-Amplitude Modulation, paragraph 2; Figure 5 B and D
outcomes.quote: During profound unconsciousness, i.e., from 10–40 min after LOC, the phase–amplitude modulation shifted by 180°, such that the alpha/beta amplitudes were largest at the peaks of low-frequency oscillations (Fig. 5 B and D; P < 0.05 in 8 of 10 subjects by permutation test
outcomes.notes: As fig5-trough-max-induction, 10 to 40 min after LOC.

outcomes.statement: During emergence, the modulation reverted to trough-max about 15 min before ROC, significant in 9 of 10 subjects.
outcomes.source: Results, Different Patterns of Phase-Amplitude Modulation, paragraph 2; Figure 5B
outcomes.quote: During emergence, the phase–amplitude modulation reverted to the trough-max pattern at ∼15 min before ROC (Fig. 5B; P < 0.05 in 9 of 10 subjects, permutation test)
outcomes.notes: As fig5-trough-max-induction, aligned at ROC (not deposited).

outcomes.statement: The low-frequency phase modulates a broad range of higher frequencies, from theta through gamma, in both the trough-max and the peak-max regimes.
outcomes.source: Figure S3; SI Materials and Methods; Results, Different Patterns of Phase-Amplitude Modulation, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: These results show that the low-frequency oscillation modulates a broad range of higher frequencies spanning theta through gamma bands in both the trough-max and peak-max regimes
outcomes.notes: The epochs are centred at LOC and LOC + 30 min (LOC not deposited) and averaged across 10 subjects (1 deposited); no channel names for Fz (metadata_insufficient).

findings.statement: The dandiset holds one subject (sub-Subject001), where the paper and the dandiset's own description report ten volunteers. Dandisets 001286 and 001287 carry the same description of the study and hold no files. Searching DANDI for propofol, Purdon, Yousefi, anesthesia, consciousness, Emery Brown and EEG found no other dandiset with these data.

The behavioural task is not deposited (stimulus times and types, button presses), nor the infusion levels and their times, nor the behavioural markers EON, LOC, ROC and EOFF. Every finding of the paper is defined from or aligned to these, so none can be tested.

The 64 EEG channels have no names, positions or bad-channel marks; the file has no electrode table, although the paper digitized each subject's electrode positions. The frontal channel the paper analyses, the Laplacian reference and every spatial result need them. Nine channels have SDs above 300 uV, which suggests noisy channels the paper would have excluded.

The EEG is stored as a generic TimeSeries (named example_timeseries, description "no description") with data of shape 64 x 2,316,950, channels first. NWB puts time on the first axis, so pynwb reports 64 samples. The series is not an ElectricalSeries and has no electrodes.

The subject's age is P30D (30 days) for a volunteer the paper describes as 18 to 36 years old. The session start time (2025-01-10T14:24:38Z) equals the file creation date, the date of the conversion, not of the recording. The identifier (NWB123) and session description (EEG Session Example) are placeholders, and the ORCID in the file's notes (0000-0001-2345-6789) differs from the contact's ORCID on DANDI (0009-0006-8777-8262).
Subject001 is not linked to the paper's numbering of its ten subjects (for example subject 7, shown in Figure 1), so the deposited recording cannot be matched to any per-subject result of the paper.

The values are consistent with the description where they can be checked. The 60 Hz mains peak and the roll-off above 100 Hz fit the stated 250 Hz rate, the amplitudes fit microvolts, no channel duplicates another, there are no gaps, and the band-power time course (beta rising at minutes 17 and 33, low-frequency and alpha power high from minute 48 to minute 97) has the outline of a gradual propofol induction and emergence, against a reference period (minutes 0 to 15) chosen after looking at the data. The duration does not match. The described protocol (a 20-min baseline, ten 14-min levels and 20 min after the infusion) implies about 180 min, and the file holds 154.5 min; the file marks none of the protocol's phases, so which part is shorter or missing cannot be told.
